items.explanation: Ernest Hemingway's World War I novel A Farewell to Arms (1929) is structured into five books, mirroring the five-act structure of a classical tragedy as it follows Frederic Henry and Catherine Barkley from the Italian front to Switzerland.

items.explanation: These lines from Geoffrey Chaucer's General Prologue to The Canterbury Tales describe the Wife of Bath and are written in a heroic couplet—a pair of rhyming iambic pentameter lines, a form Chaucer pioneered in English verse.

structured.options_hint: George Eliot Virginia Woolf Irish Murdoc

items.explanation: In her feminist essay A Room of One's Own (1929), Virginia Woolf invents Judith Shakespeare, a fictional equally gifted sister of William Shakespeare, to illustrate how patriarchal society denied women education and artistic opportunity.

items.stem:

Reason (R) : They are called so, because Dickens adulates in these novels the careers and adventures of criminals.

structured.lead: Given below are two statements:

statements.label: Reason (R)
statements.text: They are called so, because Dickens adulates in these novels the careers and adventures of criminals

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation.

items.explanation: While Dickens's early crime fiction such as Oliver Twist (1837–1838) was grouped with the 1830s 'Newgate school' of fiction dealing with London criminals, Dickens explicitly refused to glamorize or adulate criminal life, portraying its grim squalor and moral consequences instead (making Reason R false).

structured.options_hint: John Lyly Thomas Nashe George Peele Thom

items.explanation: The University Wits were late-16th-century Elizabethan playwrights educated at Oxford (Lyly, Peele, Lodge) or Cambridge (Marlowe, Greene, Nashe). Although sometimes loosely grouped with them, Thomas Kyd attended Merchant Taylors' School and never went to a university.

items.title: Q15 · Dec 2011 (Paper II)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem:
A foot consisting of a strong syllable
followed by a weak syllable is called

structured.lead: A foot consisting of a strong syllable followed by a weak syllable is called
structured.options_hint: Trochee Iambic Spondee Terza Rima

items.explanation: In English prosody, a trochee (or trochaic foot) is a two-syllable metrical foot consisting of a stressed (strong) syllable followed by an unstressed (weak) syllable, the exact reverse of an iamb.

structured.lead:
What is it that Chaucer focuses on in the depiction of the Wife of Bath in
The Canterbury Tales ?
structured.options_hint: Meekness Defiance Chastity Experience

items.explanation: Chaucer centres his depiction of Alison, the Wife of Bath, on lived 'Experience' as opposed to clerical 'auctoritee' (authority). Her Prologue famously opens, 'Experience, though noon auctoritee / Were in this world, is right ynogh for me.'

structured.lead: A 'curtal sonnet' consists of
structured.options_hint: 11 lines 12 lines 13 lines 14 lines

items.explanation: Invented by Gerard Manley Hopkins and used in poems like 'Pied Beauty' and 'Peace,' a curtal sonnet is a curtailed 11-line (ten-and-a-half-line) sonnet consisting of a six-line stanza followed by a four-and-a-half-line stanza ending in a tail-piece.

items.explanation: Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot (1953) is subtitled 'A tragicomedy in two acts' (corresponding to the fourth option where 'two' was omitted in printing). Its symmetrical two-act structure underscores the repetitive circularity of Vladimir and Estragon's waiting.

items.stem: James Joyce's Exiles is a

structured.lead: James Joyce's Exiles is a
structured.options_hint: Short Story Poem Play Novel

items.explanation: Exiles (1918) is James Joyce's only extant play. Influenced by Henrik Ibsen, the three-act drama explores marital fidelity, jealousy, and emotional freedom through the writer Richard Rowan and his wife Bertha in Dublin.

items.stem:
The expression, "dreaming house" is
an example of

structured.lead: The expression, "dreaming house" is an example of
structured.options_hint: Zeugma Transferred epithet Chiasmus Apos

items.explanation: 'Dreaming house' is an example of a transferred epithet (hypallage), in which an adjective or participle describing a human state ('dreaming') is grammatically shifted from the people inside to the inanimate house itself.

structured.lead: The term 'Practical Criticism' is coined by
structured.options_hint: William Empson Wimsatt, Jr Richards Leav

items.explanation: I. A. Richards coined and popularized the term in his landmark book Practical Criticism: A Study of Literary Judgment (1929), based on his Cambridge experiments asking students to analyze 'blind' poems stripped of authorial and historical context.

items.explanation: Viktor Shklovsky was a founding theorist of Russian Formalism and the OPOJAZ group in St. Petersburg. In his seminal 1917 essay 'Art as Technique,' he introduced the concept of ostranenie (defamiliarization).
